title: Hard k-CNF instances for PPSZ with small resolution width and near-2/k savings upper bound

standard_prerequisites.name: Large-girth regular graphs, Hall's theorem and the Atserias-Dalmau resolution-width game characterization
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Formal Erdős–Sachs[4] regular-graph existence and Atserias–Dalmau Theorem9[2] remain cited standard prerequisites. The paper's common-lift proof is completely retained in AppendixA rather than merely cited. All12 original bibliography entries retained.

core_obligations: Preserve the precise bounded-resolution PPSZ heuristic R_w, random ordering/guess semantics, all k/epsilon/m quantifiers, width w<=sqrt(epsilon loglog(m)/(2log(k)))-3 and polynomial-prefactor success upper bound.
Retain full hard-instance graph construction, zero-charge Tseitin and bridge formulas, local injectivity/covering assumptions, unique-assignment observation and common-lift AppendixA.

Retain complete PPSZ-to-resolution-width reduction and expander extraction proof, followed by the entire Delayer strategy with five invariants, three cases, blocking-cycle argument and final path splitting.
Keep author padding paragraph including its own omitted-detail statement; do not fill it in or generalize the theorem to unconditional ETH/SETH.
difficulty_reason: The non-routine mechanism uses common covers of large-girth regular graphs to build uniquely satisfiable TseitinBridge formulas, then converts excessive PPSZ forcing to an expander and defeats bounded-width resolution via a path-maintaining Delayer strategy with blocking and splitting cases.
